The late-read witness (Witness.Stale.devalued_read_late_locks_up) meets the letter of past-turning-back's test ("a reading or act comes too late: kept for good although read ... a deadline missed") while involving no loss at all: what is taken up late is a change in the weights the rule itself goes by. The test's wording does not say whether a loss is required; the gloss does ("what is being lost"). If past-turning-back is meant only for a loss read too late, its test could say so; if a late-taken change of the rule's own weights also belongs there, this witness is a candidate for a witness-strength mark on that place, traced to devalued_read_late_locks_up rather than to this exit's cited law. Also, the holds-itself gloss says "what gets chosen next is set by what has been chosen most"; in these witnesses the held option can be the one chosen less often (3:2 held for the second, because it is weighted double), so "most" holds only after weighting.

1. This dynamic's home state (a counter-rule rebuilt from its own results, held as the rule it replaced was) is holds-itself; the dynamic adds no place of its own. Its two remaining declarations that are not exits (Alternating.never_locked: from a start against the rule, held neither way at any step; uniform_locks: held from any start by the step after the second rebuilding) are entries INTO or failures to enter holds-itself and are not listed as items, so the map will not show that a counter-rule may never settle (never_locked is a witness that fits several-ways only loosely: the lead and the rule fall in alternation, nothing tipping). 2. Exit 2 exposes a gap between holds-itself, uncounted and judged-inside: the state 'held in place while a loss the rule does not register grows, with only the rule (not also the way it is judged) rebuilt from the winners' (ClosedCapture.lock_outlives_loss) fits none of the three tests cleanly. holds-itself's test says the law says NOTHING about a loss; judged-inside's test requires the rule AND its judging both formed from the winners; uncounted's test does not mention the hold. Two of three readers resolved this by starting exit 2 from judged-inside, one from holds-itself; I used holds-itself because this dynamic's own laws are RuleCapture's. If the closed-capture dynamic's lock_outlives_loss is placed in judged-inside or uncounted, the same turned_by_loss arrow will leave from there too, and the map should show these as one law leaving from more than one origin rather than as separate findings. 3. turned_by_loss holds from any start whatever the lead, so cost-counts is reachable under that change of law from every place where a loss grows each step; the arrow's origin on the map is a choice of the dynamic citing it, not something the theorem fixes.

One gap in the list showed on exit 2. turned_by_loss takes a growing loss (Accrues) as a premise, so the situation just before its change of law is 'a rule rebuilt from its own results and held, while a loss it does not count grows' (ClosedCapture.lock_outlives_loss, whose rule is read from the share through hA alone). No place's test fits that exactly: holds-itself says the law says nothing of a loss; judged-inside asks that the rule AND the way it is judged both come from the winners; uncounted is about being selected alike whatever happens outside. For this dynamic holds-itself is right because the entry cites only the laws of the rule alone (uniform_locks, locked_stays), but the same law (turned_by_loss) will be drawn from judged-inside for closed-capture, so the map will carry two arrows into cost-counts by one theorem whose statement holds from any start. Worth one line on the map: this way out is proved from every start; the origin shown is the entry's, not the theorem's. Also: this entry and habit-lock-in-active-inference are the only two entries with standing 'reading' whose exits cite proved laws; I kept the exits' own strengths (witness, sufficient) because a law shows each, and the reading is only that an actual counter-rule is a case. If the pass wants one policy for such items, it needs to be the same for both entries.

1. A place is missing for what a shared way can no longer tell apart (a difference merged away, or regained). Exits 4 and 5 are both about it (outside_returns, coined_returns), and so are laws of this dynamic that are not exits (impose_loses_iff: each loses exactly the differences its own way drew that the imposed one merges; source_loses_nothing). It is close in kind to 'uncounted' but no rule here scores anything, so I did not force it; exit 4 is given as leads-out and exit 5 as inside all-on-one. 2. all-on-one's gloss says "Another returns only from outside or by being newly made". For this dynamic the 'newly made' half is not a return of a second way in use: by coined_returns with broadcast_reaches, a newly made word heard by all leaves everyone on the same one, with a merged difference restored. Only the 'from outside' half (exit 2, with exit 3 as its necessary condition) leads to several-ways. 3. all-on-one's test says 'all members'. Exit 2's law is about an agreeing group that may have others outside it; where the group is everyone, all_agree_rest says it never leaves under hearing. The map should say 'a group all on one, while another way is still in use elsewhere' for the arrow out, or readers will take it that agreement of everyone can dissolve from within. 4. several-ways' test says 'no law in play keeps one in place', which is right, but this dynamic has a proved stay there that is not listed as an exit: never_agrees_of_both and TwoFormations.crossing_never_agrees (a rule favouring neither party nor way never settles a symmetric disagreement), and Path.never_agree (being connected is not enough). If the map shows stays, several-ways has one here. 5. This dynamic has no rule rebuilt from its results and no loss reaching a rule, so holds-itself and felt (one reader's votes on exits 2-5) do not apply to any of its items.

Three things in the place list showed up while checking this dynamic. (1) all-on-one is labelled 'Everyone on the same one', but the laws that say what leaving needs (run_kept_iff, outside_needed, outside_returns) are about a GROUP that agrees while someone outside may hold another way; when the group is literally everyone, nothing leaves under hearing (all_agree_rest). The gloss already says 'another returns only from outside', so the place is meant as a group with an outside; the label or gloss should say so ('everyone in the group'), or exit 2's arrow reads as a contradiction. The same population is then several-ways as a whole and all-on-one for the group: the map needs to say whose agreement a node is. (2) No place names what a shared way can no longer tell apart, or its return. This dynamic has four laws about it (impose_loses_iff, source_loses_nothing, outside_returns, coined_returns); exits 4 and 5 land outside the 15 for that reason. It is close in kind to 'uncounted' but no rule is rebuilt from results here and no one's say is involved, so it was rightly not forced there. (3) 'exact' on exit 1 is exact over every start, not for a given start; an arrow label that drops 'from any start' turns a true iff into a false one. Also not among the exits though proved in the same file: never_agrees_of_both (a rule treating both parties and both ways alike never brings a symmetric disagreement to agree), which is a 'stays' in several-ways and the general law beside exit 6's witness.

1. all-on-one's test asks that 'the law says what staying or leaving needs'. Both witnesses here state only arrival at step 1 (two agents, two words); neither says the shared word stays. The arrows are drawn as arrivals by witness; the test as written is stricter than what these items carry. 2. several-ways is carrying two different starts here: 'no one has any word yet' (exit 1) and 'one has a word, the other none' (exit 2). Neither is literally 'several ways in use'; a reader of the map may want the label or gloss to cover 'not yet shared' explicitly, or exit 2's start will look mis-placed. 3. The dynamic's headline laws (Becoming.CountedCodes.never_shared, never_shared_of_involution, shared_no_unique_greatest: under a law and start that treat the two agents and the words alike, the two never hold one word as each one's uniquely greatest) are a 'stays in several-ways' statement with a stated condition, but they are not exits, transitions or compose entries in the atlas entry, so no item carries them onto the map. The two witness arrows are precisely the two ways that condition is dropped (the entry's 'drops' fields). Without the stays-law shown, the map shows two ways out of several-ways and not the proved reason one does not leave it otherwise. 4. This dynamic is family C (codes between two communicating agents), with valence 'none asserted'; nothing in it concerns a rule rebuilt from its results or a loss. Its link to the capture chain is only through the several-ways / all-on-one pair.

several-ways is doing double duty here: (1) two ways each in use, (2) none yet, and, for exit 2, (3) one member already leaning while another holds nothing. Its gloss says \"nothing has tipped toward any of them\", which case (3) strains. If the map keeps exit 2 as drawn, the gloss could read \"...and not everyone has come to one\" or the arrow's condition must always be shown with it. Also: this dynamic's main proved law (Becoming.CountedCodes.never_shared: under a rule that treats the words alike, from an even start, the two never hold one word) is a \"stays in several-ways\" item with strength above witness, but it is a declaration, not an exit or transition, so it is not among the items; the two witness arrows out of several-ways are drawn without the proved law that says when one stays there. all-on-one's test asks that \"the law says what staying or leaving needs\"; neither witness says anything about staying (each states step 1 only).

1. A destination is missing: the hold left because what is used up falls on the winners themselves, nobody having noticed it (exit 3, Borne.shapers_left; the general laws are borne_by_shapers_favours_iff and borne_falls). cost-counts's test requires that the loss be noticed ('BECAUSE the loss is read'), which this witness excludes by construction; shaping-costs's test requires a practice of bending the rule, while the record only writes the loss as an added cost in that lever. Either cost-counts's test could admit 'or the loss enters the count itself by falling on the winners', or shaping-costs's could admit a loss borne by the winners; as the list stands, three readers drew three different arrows and I marked it leads-out. The mirror law (borne by the others: a return to the winners, the hold stays closed, closed_stays_closed / Borne.others_locked) has no exit in this dynamic's data at all.
2. Three tests claim one law. window_never_read concludes 'locked at every later step' (holds-itself), 'the loss passes every bound' while the rule is made from the lead alone (judged-inside), under 'removed before they read' (noticers-gone). I placed it by its distinguishing premise (noticers-gone); the readers' split on exit 1 and transition 1 follows this overlap. The tests would separate better if holds-itself, judged-inside and noticers-gone each said which premise or conclusion decides.
3. noticers-gone against past-turning-back: Drained.strong_undone (noticed twice, then the hold kept for good) matches past-turning-back's 'kept for good although read' as literally as it matches noticers-gone's 'removed'. The item's kind is 'window or deadline', and past-turning-back's test also lists 'a deadline missed', which window_never_read (removed before they register it) could be read as. The record itself says the step past which the window can no longer turn the course is not shown, so I kept both at noticers-gone.
4. cost-counts covers two different endings that the map may want told apart: turned and held the other way while the noticers still stand, and (clock_turned) turned by noticers who are then themselves removed, the other side afterwards held by the count-only rule alone.
5. This dynamic's transition is a fork between two outcomes of one start, not a change from its between.from to its between.to; transitions of kind 'window or deadline' elsewhere may need the same reading before any arrow is drawn from their 'between' field.

Two things this dynamic shows about the list. (1) No place holds 'the loss falls on the winners themselves and the hold is left with nobody noticing' (exit 3, and the iff laws borne_by_shapers_favours_iff / borne_by_others_favours_iff of on-whom-the-loss-falls). cost-counts fits by its gloss ('enters what the rule goes by') but its test says 'BECAUSE the loss is read'; the record's own correspondence reads this case as polluter-pays, an internalised cost. If the list is revised, either widen cost-counts' test to 'read, or borne by the winners in what the rule counts', or add a place; until then exit 3 leads out. (2) The record's counterexample Drained.strong_undone (felt to noticers-gone, witness: those who would notice judge against the winners twice, are removed with the winners still ahead, and the hold is back for good from step 3) sits only inside transition 1's declarations and is carried by no exit, so under one-decision-per-item it reaches the map only as a note. It is the counterweight to exit 2's arrow from the same start and should get an item of its own. Smaller: for 'necessary' exits decided as 'stays', the copied strength is about leaving while the stated condition is about staying; exit 1's fixed wording says both, and the same care is needed wherever that pairing occurs.

1. shaping-costs / shaping-pays are labelled 'Bending the rule costs / pays', but what the laws put there is wider: any practice whose doers leave a + s and the others a + c, falling or not by c against s. This dynamic's two proved cases are giving back to one's own kind against keeping (transition 1) and forgiving one slip against answering it (transition 2). Neither is something a person would call bending the rule in one's own favour, yet both are on these two places by a proved identity of counts. Either the gloss should say so ('a costly practice, shaping the rule being the chapter's case, pays its doers or does not'), or family E's cases should hang on the costs/pays arrow as named cases rather than as arrows of their own. 2. The layer lacks a mark for 'the same place seen in another model' (a proved identification, no change). Both compose entries here are exactly that; forced into the five decisions they come out unresolved, which undersells them, since they are proved. 3. The list has no place for 'how far like is paired with like': transition 3 (mixed pairs) turns on it, and so, in shaping-the-rule, does the grouped law. With β < γ fixed, more like-pairing cannot help (answering_never_rises); with γ < β it decides. That is a real condition of family E/C with nowhere to sit on this region's map. 4. These arrows are sides of a supplied parameter read in one cohort ('no law here is of a course of cohorts'; 'Which sign β − γ has: both factors are supplied'). A map legend should distinguish such both-ways threshold arrows from arrows where the dynamic itself carries something across in time.

1. The tie. shaping-pays is defined weakly ('at least what it costs', 'numbers do not fall') and shaping-costs strictly ('numbers fall'). Every arrow between them should carry its condition in the weak form on the pays side ('at least'), or the tie is left unplaced; both arrows of this dynamic had the strict form and transition 2's Chinese said the tie loses. Worth checking on the other dynamics' costs/pays arrows. 2. Cases. Transitions 1 and 2 are the one threshold of shaping-the-rule's transition 1 (cost at most what comes back to the doers alone), reached by proved identities of counts. Three sources, one arrow: the map should show cases on an arrow, not parallel arrows. 3. The label. 'Bending the rule in one's own favour' (example: lobbying) fits those who give to givers, and still less pairs that forgive a slip, only through the identity of counts; in the theory's terms they are 'shapers' because what they do sets what each kind leaves. A lay reader will not see reciprocity or forgiveness as bending a rule. Either the place's gloss gains a line ('any costly practice whose return can come back to its doers alone'), or these cases are shown beside the arrow with their own plain sentence. 4. A missing mark. The two compose entries are proved 'same place seen in another model' links; the five decision types have no slot for them, so they land in unresolved although nothing about them is unresolved. 5. The mixed group (transition 3) is family E's own ground: giving that waits, by how far like is paired with like and how long the run is. It cannot be put under the region's grouped law in general (the counts are of that form only where the run is one step or the two returns are equal, by my own arithmetic check, not a Lean theorem). The region's 15 places have no place for it.

This dynamic belongs to family H and mostly lies outside the capture chain; only its fourth exit touches the region. Its own condition has no place among the 15: 'still going, so it never used up what it lives on faster than that came back' (Flow.persists_never_overdraws, Flow.member_after_never_overdrew). Nor does the origin of its one lawful exit: 'using up what it depends on faster than it is renewed, from a short stock', which leads by a sufficient law to the listed place 'ended' (GroupEnding.Flow.coupled_generation_childless). 'uncounted' is not that place: its test is about what lies outside what reaches a rule, and the ending law has no rule and does not ask that the thing drawn be uncounted. If the map wants 'ended' to have a lawful way in from this side, it needs a place such as 'living past what renews it' (shared with families A, B and H); otherwise exit 1 stays undrawn. Exits 2 and 3 lead to conditions of other regions (keeping whatever keeps one going, an overseer's assent included; fixed only on the cases met, family D) and both are readings.

Two observations for whoever revises the place list. (1) This dynamic's own condition has no place: 'still going, so it never used up what it lives on faster than it came back'. With a place for 'using up what it lives on faster than it comes back' (no rule or judge involved), exit 1 becomes a sufficient one-way arrow to 'ended' (GroupEnding.Flow.coupled_generation_childless), and Flow.persists_never_overdraws becomes a 'stays'. 'uncounted' cannot stand in for it because its test asks for something outside what reaches a rule, and these laws have no rule. (2) The test of 'holds-itself' excludes any law that speaks of a loss outside what is counted. A locked state in which such a loss is being drawn while those who would notice are still present but have not yet registered it (the start of PoolFromCourse.window_never_read and of 02 §10's reading) then has no clean home: it is not holds-itself by that clause, not noticers-gone yet, and not judged-inside until they are gone. The earlier readers' 2:1 split on exit 4's origin comes from this, and the same question will decide the origin of the lawful arrow in the-lock-draws-its-readers-out, transition 1.

1. Transition 1 is one threshold with two heads out of 'uncounted' (to 'felt' if the first difference comes before the point of no return, to 'past-turning-back' if at or after). One decision per item cannot hold both; I returned the in-time head and put the other, equally exact, in its note. The map needs a way to draw a fork as one item. 2. 'felt' here means specifically 'a difference shows on someone with a say while the loss could still be kept'. The too-late side is also felt (the gloss of past-turning-back covers it: 'even where the loss is now plain to those bearing it'), so the two places are distinguished by timing, not by whether anyone feels it; the 'felt' gloss could say 'while it can still be kept' to keep them apart. 3. 'Can tell' in this dynamic is the earliest possible registering (readable), not an actual one: a given rule may register later or never. The place list has no way to mark that gap; it matters because uncounted → felt at 'exact' could be read as 'the rule notices'. 4. 'past-turning-back' in this dynamic is relative to a supplied set of courses still available and a supplied statement of what is to be kept (record: 'The courses compared, the feasible courses and what is kept are supplied'); in the one worked example it is a family-A tipping level (margin-of-a-regime). The node therefore has a real way out of the region toward family A that the 15 places do not show. 5. A witness of past-turning-back → ended exists (FourReaders.noReturn: the one living on the thing ends one step after the point) but the atlas carries it only in this entry's 'beyond' text, not as an exit, so no item here can draw it. 6. Exit 4 and compose 1 are 'same-as' links between two dynamics of the region; the decision vocabulary has no kind for an identification, so both are returned as unresolved though their role (letting two dynamics share the nodes 'felt' and 'past-turning-back', at the strength of a reading) is clear.

Three observations from this dynamic. (1) 'felt' and 'past-turning-back' overlap where the first difference shows on someone with a say at or after the point of no return: the loss then does reach a person with a say, but too late. The past-turning-back gloss already covers this (\"even where the loss is now plain to those bearing it\"), so on this dynamic 'felt' has to be read as 'felt while it can still be kept'. If the felt node's gloss does not say that, a reader may take exit 2's arrow to skip a place the bearers do pass through. (2) Transition 1 is a fork out of 'uncounted' decided by one exact threshold, and the one-decision-per-item shape holds only one side; the other side sits in a note. (3) 'felt' here means a rule going by these people could register the difference, not that any given rule does (ReadsInTime.readable is one-directional); the place list does not separate 'can tell' from 'does tell'.

1. No listed place fits exit 2 (a view's holders drawn below what they need, so the view moves only by people taking it up): its premise is the drawdown of families A and B, and 'ended' fits the holders' lines, not the view. 2. noticers-gone and all-on-one overlap on this dynamic: exit 6 and compose 1 (absent_step, fixed_of_present) say of the missing view what all-on-one's gloss says of the remaining one ("another returns only from outside or by being newly made"); the map may want to show that noticers-gone, seen from the views held, is all-on-one for the view that is left. 3. In the commons witness (exit 4) noticers-gone is reached only as 'one line removed and the rest outnumbered': the wide line, which also takes everything in, persists as one of three. The place's gloss covers 'outnumbered', but an arrow label should not suggest every noticer is gone. 4. Two proved pieces of this dynamic have no item and so no arrow or stay: Flow.closedFrom_of_standing (once everyone still standing holds the view and people copy only those standing, the view is closed: the step from noticers-gone toward all-on-one, which the atlas marks open for a course the acts generate) and Commons.overdrawn_spreads_then_ends (the takers overdraw their own source and are removed while the others persist: a self-limiting end of one side that is none of the 15 places as listed). 5. kept_iff is exact both ways, so it also gives what leaving all-on-one needs (a holder leaving a successor who does not hold it), but no item names where that leads; several-ways is the natural reading and is not drawn here.

Three things the place list made hard for this dynamic. (1) 'uncounted' has a gloss and example that include an unregistered thing which in fact feeds the user (the seabed that feeds the fish), while the first clause of its test ('selected alike whatever happens there') fits only the case where nothing comes back. Exit 4 fits both; exit 5 fits the gloss and example but not that clause over the whole run. I kept exit 5's origin on the gloss and example; if the test is meant strictly, exit 5 would become unresolved with 'ended' as where it seems to lead. (2) 'noticers-gone' covers both 'all gone' and 'removed and outnumbered'. Exit 4 reaches only the second: one line that takes everything in persists as one of three. A map label reading 'gone' overstates that witness unless the arrow carries the caveat. (3) There is no place for 'drawn below what it needs' (exit 2), so the law that a view stops spreading by out-breeding where its holders are drawn down has nowhere to start from in this region.

1) cost-counts versus felt for exit 1: the law's destination is 'the removal fails the measure when the measure is taken over a fixed list'. The readers split 2:1 because cost-counts' test is worded for a rule that favours winners ('no longer favours the old winners because the loss is read'), and this dynamic has no winners and no rule formed from results. A clause in cost-counts' test such as 'or the measure itself fails any history that removes someone on its list' would settle it; without it, felt will keep attracting this item although the Lean says 'turned'. 2) noticers-gone and ended can hold together: the witness clearedBack_survivors_pass shows the measure taken among those left passing a history in which everyone, the choosers included, is removed ('registers no removal, not even its own ending'). No item of this dynamic carries that as an exit (it is in the entry's 'beyond' field), so no arrow is drawn, but the map's noticers-gone gloss ('nothing shows as missing') is true even with no one left. 3) all-on-one's test says 'all members hold one form'; exit 4's law is about all who are still present after the others were removed. The place fits, but its example (a word everyone uses) does not suggest that it can be reached by removal as well as by spreading. 4) noticers-gone is held by two dynamics under two kinds of choosing (by who is still there, here; by who is ahead, in the-lock-draws-its-readers-out), joined only by argument (exit 5), not by a law; the place's 'how far seen' should say so if it is shown as one node.

Three observations from this dynamic, for whoever draws the map. (1) noticers-gone and all-on-one touch: 'holders of every other view are gone' and 'everyone left holds the one view' are one fact said two ways, so the exit-4 arrow between them is a meeting point with a law of staying behind it (closedFrom_of_standing), not a movement shown in time; the lock record states that a generated course producing it under copying is not shown. (2) This dynamic chooses by who is still there, with no rule built from winners; cost-counts' and felt's tests are worded for a rule and its winners, so exit 1 and exit 3 fit them only as 'the measure fails a history that removes anyone' and 'the loss falls on the choosers themselves'. A sentence in those places' glosses allowing 'a measure' beside 'a rule' would make the fit plain. (3) The strength scale given to readers has no value for the data's 'argued' (exit 5 here, and exit 6 and the compose entry of readings-revised-spread-and-locked); readers have written it as 'reading', 'argued' and 'stated' in different places. One agreed value would keep the map's marks consistent. Also: the only constructed case of exit 3's condition (the loss falling back on the choosers) ends with every line removed and the measure among those left still passing (Habitat.clearedBack_removes_both, clearedBack_survivors_pass), so an arrow from noticers-gone toward 'ended' as a witness exists in the Lean of this dynamic although no exit of the entry is written for it.

1. A place is missing for where exits 4 and 5 lead: 'made good again' (what was taken is given back and the outcome is as if the act had not been done; chapter 02 section 7). It is the only way out of this region that this dynamic's laws give a necessary condition for, and it passes through someone other than the doer being reached. 2. 'felt' is worded for someone whose judgment enters a rule. Exits 4 and 5 are about a responder who answers in the exchange itself, with no rule in the law; the place fits them only loosely. If 'made good again' is added, its incoming arrow may need a gloss of 'felt' wide enough for 'reached someone other than the doer who can answer'. 3. The uncounted/felt line is drawn exactly by two iff laws (exits 1 and 6), but both compare two outcomes for one fixed group. They say which side a loss is on, not that anything crosses. What moves a loss across (who joins the group, what comes to reach them) is in the witnesses (exits 2 and 3) and otherwise open in the data. A map reader should not take the two exact arrows as 'this happens'. 4. Exits 9 and 10 leave from 'felt' to two family B dynamics outside the region (several each pushing their own count; the others' taking outrunning renewal). The gloss of 'felt' already says 'it depends on how many they are and how early'; those two exits are where that sentence has its laws, and the region has no place for 'felt, and still drawn down by several each counting their own'. 5. Exit 7 and compose 1 say the blind spot covers the choice of who is asked. 'noticers-gone' lists 'never asked' in its gloss, but the data here gives only a staying (nothing favours keeping a noticer), not an arrival there.

Four things this dynamic shows about the list. (1) 'uncounted' and 'felt' are two sides of one exact boundary here (exits 1 and 6 are the same iff, by date and over the whole run); the laws compare two outcomes for one fixed group and never show a rule passing from one side to the other in time, except in the single constructed case of exit 3. A both-ways arrow drawn from them should read as a boundary. (2) There is no place for 'made good again' (exits 4 and 5), and 'felt' is used loosely there for a responder in the exchange with no rule. (3) 'noticers-gone' includes 'never asked', which is also the plain condition of 'uncounted' where the one who would notice was never on the roll; and the removal of noticers has two honest tails, 'uncounted' (from the winners' side, as this dynamic's role text has it) and 'felt' (from the whole rule's side, since the lock-draws-its-readers-out has them reading while they stand). Exit 8's arrow failed partly on that ambiguity. (4) Exit 7 and compose 1 put a second-level fact in 'uncounted': what is not registered there is whether a noticer is kept, not the loss itself.

(1) cost-counts' test ends "or the measure is bounded so the uncounted is not pushed down". Exit 1 was read as cost-counts by two readers through that clause, but in keeping_optimum_takes_slack nothing enters the rule: the allowed outcomes are limited from outside, and the uncounted is still pushed down to the limit exactly (the family takes all the slack; the atlas forbids "a constraint at the need leaving a margin above it"). The list has no place for "kept by a limit on what is allowed, while the rule still does not count it"; I put it as staying in uncounted. If the map wants it visible, it is a distinct condition from cost-counts and the test of cost-counts should say the bound is in the measure, not in the allowed set. (2) ended's gloss says "or what it needed is no longer there", which is exactly a broken dependence (Web.Broken), while its test asks that "something no longer continues at all". The two differ by a premise (activity needs support, the dependence persisting), which is why transition 1 is exact for the cut-off and only sufficient for the ending. (3) For this dynamic the thing that reaches 'ended' is the dependant outside the count, not the rule, the winners or the loop; an arrow uncounted -> ended should say whose ending it is. (4) No place for a rule that aims at a target ("enough"; chapter 03, and the neighbouring dynamic on set-point optima): exit 3 is a witness about such a rule and sits inside uncounted only through the clause "selected alike whatever happens there". (5) The uncounted gloss says the thing "is being used up"; exit 2's witness is a case in that place's test where it is not used up (the rule is indifferent and gains nothing by it), so the gloss is a little stronger than the test: with no way to turn the uncounted into what counts, nothing drives the using-up.

Two things this dynamic shows about the list. (1) 'ended' is used here for a dependant outside the count ending while the rule and its winners continue in 'uncounted'; the place's example (a fishery closed) reads as the whole activity ending. An arrow into 'ended' needs its condition to say who ends, or the place needs a second example of this kind. (2) Exit 3 (a rule satisfied at a target) has no place of its own: all three earlier readers pointed to 'enough' in chapter 03. It fits 'uncounted' by the test's first clause (scored alike whatever happens there), but 'uncounted' then covers two different rules: one that keeps pushing (drains with room) and one that stops at a target (may or may not drain). If the map should show that difference, the list lacks a place for 'a rule that aims at enough'. Also, cost-counts' clause 'the measure is bounded so the uncounted is not pushed down' can be misread as covering exit 1 (a limit on allowed outcomes); there the uncounted is still pushed to the limit, so the clause should be read as about the rule's own measure, not about a floor on outcomes.
